original_test_intent: Validate correctable RCD/DRAM parity handling for every required slot/UMC, showing an attributable corrected parity event without unintended warm reset, fatal escalation or loss of memory service.
original_method: Correct the list-command syntax through vendor authority; map physical RCD/DIMM targets to socket/die/UMC and any channel/rank selectors; confirm what `dramothererrors`, errortype 0 and errormode 1 inject; capture baseline parity/status/counters; inject one CE on one approved target; require corrected parity evidence and stable service; treat any UCE/reset/BERT record as either an explicitly approved alternate checkpoint or unexpected escalation; restore RCD parity/injection/HDT state.
manual_activity: The FAE resolves CE versus UCE/BERT scope, corrects the malformed command from vendor documentation, maps the RCD/UMC target, executes one parity stimulus and owns recovery/restoration.
required_inputs: Decision whether UCE warm-reset/BERT criterion is copied text, conditional escalation evidence or a separate checkpoint
Vendor-correct valid-UMC syntax and tool/spec version/hash/license
RCD/DIMM slot to socket/die/UMC/channel/rank map and approval/correction of 0:0:3
Meaning of dramothererrors errortype 0/errormode 1 and expected corrected parity register/MCA fields
Expected no-reset versus approved reset/BERT behavior, timeout and boot recovery
BIOS/MCA/RCD Parity before/after values, abort, OOB recovery and restoration
safety_requirements: Dedicated ECC/RCD platform with OOB console and recovery
Do not execute malformed dash text or infer its correction without vendor approval
One mapped parity event only; stop on UCE, sync flood, unexpected reset, boot failure or wrong slot
Preserve preexisting logs; if reset occurs, capture BERT/UEFI/BMC before further action
No automatic retry; disable injection and restore RCD parity/MCA/HDT state
agent_execution_scope: Validate syntax, target map, severity/BERT decision, package provenance and recovery
Collect read-only tool, parity/MCA, OS/BERT/BMC, console and health evidence

engineer_actions: Approve corrected command and parity target/tool semantics
Define exact parity event and abort/recovery oracle

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The title, step and errortype 0 describe correctable parity, but Criteria requires an uncorrectable BERT record after warm reset. The valid-UMC command contains a malformed dash, fixed tuple 0:0:3 cannot establish slot 1~N, and timeout is undefined. The adjacent UCE row already owns reset/BERT coverage.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Correctable parity purpose and literal injection family are identifiable. Engineering can resolve the copied/conditional UCE criterion and syntax, so static review completes while execution is gated.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Reliability row 52 Wistron-System RAS-00772-V003: decide whether uncorrectable warm-reset/BERT Criteria is copied text, conditional escalation evidence or a separate required checkpoint from CE; provide vendor-correct listvalidumc syntax, slot/RCD-to-socket/die/UMC/channel/rank coverage and approve/correct 0:0:3; approve tool/spec provenance and dramothererrors errortype=0/errormode=1 semantics, exact CE parity oracle, reset policy, timeout, aborts, OOB recovery and restoration.

review_improvement: Separates corrected parity from reset/BERT UCE coverage and makes malformed syntax plus physical RCD target explicit, avoiding a PASS that mixes mutually different severity outcomes.
independent_technical_reasoning: RCD parity CE should normally be judged by a corrected, attributable parity record and continued service, while BERT is firmware-provided boot-time evidence commonly relevant after disruptive errors. Requiring both without a branch definition makes any outcome ambiguous. The adjacent UCE case explicitly resets, strengthening the conclusion that severity coverage must be separated. The corrupted dash is also not harmless because blindly copied Unicode can change the CLI invocation.
